etymologies.etymologyHTML: From environment +‎ -al.

quote.citation: 2013 August 10, “Can China clean up fast enough?”, in The Economist, volume 408, number 8848:
quote.text: That worries the government, which fears that environmental activism could become the foundation for more general political opposition.

quote.citation: 2000, Henk Folmer, ‎H. Landis Gabel, Principles of Environmental and Resource Economics, page 365:
quote.text: Because consumers who are buying such productss cannot fully internalize the external utility of their purchase, prices for environmental products and other environmental innovations may be insufficiently high to cover their costs ( Kaas, 1993; Cleff and Rennings, 1999).

definitions.definition: (computing) Any factor relating to the physical environment in which hardware is operated, such as the room temperature or the number of racks used to hold equipment.
